payload.claim: The acceptance criteria for `SpecReviewSession.model` and `SpecWriterSession.model` both state explicitly: 'A turn's own joined value counts as each name in it, and an empty segment counts as none' — i.e. `_merge_models` must split a single turn's own `attempt.model` (itself possibly a comma-joined multi-model string, since one turn/result event can legitimately name several models per the runner's own join logic) into separate names. No test in `test_spec_review.py` ever passes a comma-containing value as one turn's `model` via `_named(...)`; every row in both `test_a_spec_review_session_names_each_model_its_turns_named` and `test_a_spec_writer_session_names_each_model_its_turns_named` uses single bare names per turn (e.g. 'm-7', 'm-8a'), never a joined value like 'm-a,m-b' or one with an empty segment like 'm-a,,m-b' as the spec's own notes for the agent explicitly call for. Replacing `addition.split(",")` with `[addition]` in `_merge_models` (treating a turn's own joined value as one opaque name rather than splitting it) keeps every existing test green while breaking the documented per-turn-splitting and empty-segment-skipping behavior for any real turn whose result event names more than one model.
